verdict.rationale: Composio's triggers docs say that when something happens in a connected app (Slack message, GitHub commit, incoming email), a trigger sends the event as a structured payload. Composio POSTs every trigger event to a project-registered webhook URL, signed for verification, so the agent receives events instead of polling. missing for 10: documentation of how to enable or subscribe to specific trigger types per connected account or user, and independent or hands-on corroboration that trigger delivery works.

support.subject: As a developer, I can subscribe my agent to events from connected downstream apps (triggers/webhooks) instead of polling them

citations.quote: When something happens in a connected app (a new Slack message, a GitHub commit, an incoming email), a trigger sends that event to your app as a structured payload.
You register it once per project, and Composio `POST`s every trigger event there, signed so you can verify it.
